faqs.question: What is a UN-approved transportation container?
faqs.answer: It's a stainless steel container, design-approved under ADR, RID, IMDG Code, ICAO-TI, and GGVSEB, for the safe and legally compliant transport of hazardous liquids by truck, train, ship, or airplane.

faqs.question: Is this different from the in-plant Safety Can, Canister, or Barrel?
faqs.answer: Yes, though it's the same form factor: these are the transport-certified versions of those exact products, approved for movement outside the plant, where the in-plant versions are not.

faqs.question: Which transport modes does this container cover?
faqs.answer: Road under ADR, rail under RID, sea under the IMDG Code, air under ICAO-TI, and German national transport under GGVSEB, all on the same approved design.

faqs.question: How do I find the transport-certified version of my in-plant container?
faqs.answer: Match your current container type and size: a 5-liter in-plant Safety Can corresponds to the 5-liter transportation can (order number 05T), and a 10-liter in-plant Canister corresponds to the 10-liter transportation canister (10KT).

faqs.question: Does the transport container include a pressure control valve?
faqs.answer: Not as standard. The base screw cap ships without a pressure control valve; a version with one is available separately.

faqs.question: Can I get a transport-certified version of a 50-liter or larger Barrel?
faqs.answer: Not in this confirmed range — the transportation barrel is only available at 10 and 25 liters. For larger volumes, confirm directly with Inkarp.

faqs.question: How do I know which certification applies to my shipment?
faqs.answer: Match your transport mode: ADR for road, RID for rail, IMDG Code for sea, ICAO-TI for air; a shipment using multiple modes is covered by all the relevant standards on the same container.

faqs.question: Is this container reusable?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's explicitly built to be reused across shipments, helping avoid one-way, non-returnable transport packaging.

faqs.question: What packaging group is this container licensed for?
faqs.answer: It's licensed for all types of hazardous goods under packaging group X, as specified in its approval.

faqs.question: What is the price of the Transportation Containers with UN-Approval in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on the form factor, size, and whether you need the pressure valve version. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your shipment requirements are confirmed.

longForm.heroLead: Most transport certifications cover one route. This one covers all of them. Design approved to ADR for road, RID for rail, the IMDG Code for sea, ICAO-TI for air, and GGVSEB for German national transport law — the same container is certified across trucks, trains, ships, and airplanes. It's built from stainless steel, 0.6 to 1.2 mm, chemically resistant, with a removable flame trap and PTFE gaskets. The screw cap ships without a pressure control valve as standard, with a pressure-valve version also available. This isn't a separate product line. It's the transport-certified version of the Safety Can, Safety Canister, and Safety Barrel already in your plant — same form factors, licensed for the road instead of confined to it. Reusable, rather than a one-way package you dispose of after a single trip.

sections.title: Transportation Containers with UN-Approval at a Glance
sections.description: Everything you need to evaluate these containers: which international standards they're approved to, how they map to your existing in-plant containers, what sizes and order numbers exist, and Inkarp installation and service support.
body: ADR, RID, IMDG Code, ICAO-TI, and GGVSEB together cover road, rail, sea, air, and German national transport law, all on the same container.

This isn't a new product family. It's the same can, canister, and barrel form factors already in the Rötzmeier range, re-engineered and approved specifically for transport rather than confined to in-plant use.
The pressure valve is optional here, not default. The base screw cap ships without one; a pressure-control-valve version is available separately, a genuine difference from the in-plant lines.
It's built to be reused, not thrown away. Explicitly positioned to help avoid one-way, non-returnable transport packaging.

Sizing follows the in-plant lines, mostly. Cans run 1 to 5 liters, canisters 5 to 20 liters, matching their in-plant counterparts closely - but the transport barrel only reaches 25 liters, well short of the in-plant Barrel's 200-liter ceiling.

Construction stays consistent with the rest of the range. Chemically resistant stainless steel, PTFE gaskets, and a removable flame trap, the same core safety approach used across Cans, Canisters, and Barrels.

Configuration note: Confirmed line is Rötzmeier Safety Transportation Containers, UN-approved. Approved to: ADR, RID, IMDG Code, ICAO-TI, GGVSEB. Available as transportation cans (1-5 L), canisters (5-20 L), and barrels (10-25 L). Screw cap standard, without pressure control valve; pressure-valve version also available. Full specifications (exact dimensions, weight, further certification detail) are available on request from Inkarp.

sections.title: Technical Specifications
body: The technical specifications of the Transportation Containers with UN-Approval include five-standard UN approval, 0.6 to 1.2 mm construction, and a confirmed 1 to 25-liter range.
Five separate regulatory frameworks apply, depending on how the container actually travels, and this design is approved under all of them at once.

ADR covers road transport across Europe; RID covers rail; the IMDG Code governs sea freight; ICAO-TI applies to air transport; and GGVSEB is the German national law governing dangerous goods carriage. A shipment that changes transport mode partway through, truck to ship, for example, doesn't need a different container for each leg.
